newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 14.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

As Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind was set to meet his U.S., French and Canadian counterparts in Paris today over proposed military action to be taken over the humanitarian crisis in Zaire, rebel leaders from eastern Zaire warned that any troops from former colonial powers in Africa will be attacked.
SAINSBURY TO AXE BIG BANKS' CASH MACHINES

With the launch of its own bank next year, supermarkets giant Sainsbury will axe hundreds of cashpoint machines from its stores operated by the "big four' high street banks. Sainsbury-Bank of Scotland ATMs will be installed alongside Barclays, Lloyds TSB, Natwest and Midland machines, replacing underperforming ATMs.

John Fairfax newspaper group reported a 51 percent fall in first quarter profits. The Australian company blamed a stagnating economy and a lack of employment advertising for pre-tax profits of 16.3 million Australian dollars (8 million stg).
HIGHFIELD SET TO GRAB 45 MILLION STG VAUX HOMES

Pubs and hotels group Vaux, may have found a buyer for its subsidiary St Andrews nursing homes, in the private nursing homes company Highfield, which has received financial backing from the Bank of Scotland and venture capital company Apax. The purchase price is expected to be 45 million stg.
COCA-COLA IS POISED TO BOTTLE UP BRITAIN

Coca-Cola is set to receive backing for its buy-out of its partner Cadbury-Schweppes British bottling business, Coca-Cola Schweppes Beverages. The 700 million stg deal currently being studied by the EC would give Coke through its 42 percent owned partner Coca-Cola Enterprises a 15 year hold in Britain on Cadburys-Schweppes soft drinks market.
